report.verdict: Massachusetts is a ~$2.0bn (LTM taxable gaming revenue) mature, closed, high-margin market whose growth engine has downshifted: 9M 2026 sports handle rose only 2.0% to $5.99bn (online $5.93bn), with taxable sports revenue +6.0% to $611m carried entirely by hold expansion (10.2% vs 9.8%), while land-based casino GGR fell 2.4% to $880m on Encore weakness. The commercial picture is a DraftKings/FanDuel fortress (74.5% of handle, 78.5% of revenue) under a regulator that is now the most interventionist in the US on bettor limits and enforcement, with a live 51%-tax / prop-ban bill (S.302) and no iGaming path before 2027 — attractive for incumbents' margins, unattractive for a new entrant.
summary: **Market size and shape — ~$2.05bn LTM taxable gaming revenue, 9M 2026 $1,491m (+0.8% YoY).** Composed of $611.4m taxable sports wagering revenue (GGR-basis, +6.0%) and $879.8m land-based casino GGR (-2.4%). Sports is now 41.0% of the regulated base (38.7% a year ago); there is no legal online casino. Source: MGC September 2026 and September 2025 revenue reports, summed Jan–Sep.

**Sports handle growth has effectively stalled: 9M 2026 handle $5,994m, +2.0% YoY; online $5,927m, +2.3%.** Quarterly: Q1 $2,132m (-1.4%), Q2 $1,926m (+2.5%), Q3 $1,937m (+5.5%). September 2026 handle was $772.9m, -3.4% YoY — the first September decline since the March 2023 launch. FY2025 handle was $8,529m, so 2026 is tracking roughly flat-to-low-single-digit growth.

**Revenue is outgrowing handle purely on hold: 9M hold 10.20% vs 9.82% (+38bp); September hold 9.21% vs 6.54%.** Taxable sports revenue rose 6.0% to $611.4m and September revenue jumped 36.0% to $71.2m on a smaller handle — classic parlay/SGP mix and favourable results, not volume. Treat the 9M growth rate as fragile: Q2 revenue was -1.0% YoY even with a 10.7% hold.

**Online is the whole sports market: 98.9% of handle and 99.1% of taxable revenue.** Retail (three casino sportsbooks) took $67.3m handle in 9M 2026 (-19.4%) for $5.2m revenue; September retail handle fell 37.7%. Retail sports is commercially irrelevant except as the tether for casino-linked online skins.

**A two-operator fortress: DraftKings 49.5% of handle / 50.8% of revenue; FanDuel 24.9% / 27.6% (combined 74.5% / 78.5%).** Fanatics is the only material share-taker (#3, 9.9% of handle, handle +34.5% YoY); BetMGM 7.7% (-3.2%), Caesars 3.4%, theScore Bet (ex-ESPN Bet) 2.8% (-11.9%), Bally Bet 0.6%. DraftKings' home-state advantage and 10.5% hold give it $312m of 9M revenue in one state.

**Land-based casinos are flat-to-down: 9M GGR $879.8m (-2.4%).** Encore Boston Harbor $529.2m (-4.7%; September -22.1% to $46.1m, both tables and slots down), MGM Springfield $214.6m (+1.1%), Plainridge Park slots parlor $136.0m (+1.1%). September casino GGR of $82.7m (-13.6%) was the weakest September since 2020. MGC publishes no commentary; the Encore drop is unexplained and a watch item.

**Tax regime — GGR-based, no promotional deductions, with negative-month carry-forward.** Online sports (Category 3) 20% of adjusted gross sports wagering receipts; retail (Cat 1/2) 15%; Category 1 resort casinos 25% of GGR; Category 2 slots parlor 49%; DFS 15% of net adjusted receipts. Effective 9M rates: sports 19.96%, casino 28.7% (blend). Federal 0.25% excise is deductible; promo credits are not (per 23N §3 definition quoted in the MGC glossary).

**Tax take 9M 2026 $374.6m (+0.5%): sports $122.0m (+6.0%), casino $252.6m (-2.0%).** Plainridge pays $66.7m on $136m GGR (49% rate) versus MGM Springfield's $53.6m on $215m. September alone: $38.4m total (+1.6%). FY2025 sports tax was ~$168m; the 51% proposal would, on 2025 revenue, lift it to ~$430m (estimate, static).

**Licensing is closed and capped.** Expanded Gaming Act 2011 (G.L. c.23K): max three Category 1 resort casinos (only two awarded — Region C never licensed) and one Category 2 slots parlor. Sports Wagering Act 2022 (G.L. c.23N): up to 15 online licences — 8 tethered to land-based partners (2 per casino, 1 per racetrack) and 7 untethered — but only 7 online books are live, so roughly 8 slots sit unused [slot arithmetic unverified this session]. Licence fee is $5m per 5-year term [unverified this session]; first licences expire 2028, putting renewals on a 2027–28 timetable.

**The tax-hike / product-ban bill is live but not enacted.** Sen. John Keenan's S.302 'Bettor Health Act' cleared its Senate committee 5-0 in March 2026: online tax 20%→51%, ban on player props and in-game betting, ban on sports betting ads during televised games, affordability checks tied to account balances. No enactment was found before the 31 Jul 2026 end of formal session [status unverified]; expect a refile in January 2027 with the same sponsor and a more receptive AG.

**iGaming is off the table until at least the 2027–28 session.** H.4431 (Rep. Muradian), which would have created Chapter 23O and let the three casino licensees offer online slots/tables via the MGC, was sent to study by the Joint Committee on Economic Development and Emerging Technologies on 16 Mar 2026 — procedurally dead. Sweepstakes casinos remain unregulated and untouched; the MGC says it does not regulate them.

**Prediction markets are being pushed out — a defensive positive for licensees.** AG Campbell sued Kalshi (Sept 2025); Suffolk Superior Court granted a preliminary injunction (20 Jan 2026) barring sports event contracts to Massachusetts customers and denied a stay (Feb 2026); Kalshi's appeal was argued at the Supreme Judicial Court on 4 May 2026 with 38 state AGs filing in support. The SJC outcome could not be verified as of 6 Nov 2026 — it is the single biggest near-term swing factor for licensed handle.

**Enforcement is frequent, granular and public.** 13 event-catalog penalties in 2026 to date ($5,000–$25,000; MGM Springfield $25,000 in June, Caesars $10,000 in March) after a $60,000 BetMGM penalty in Dec 2025 (incl. 2,564 prohibited soccer-card wagers). The 5 Nov 2026 agenda adds briefings on Fanatics (refer-a-friend bonuses; failure to send limit notices), BetMGM (out-of-state wagers), FanDuel (proxy wagering) and penalty votes on Caesars (unauthorised events, one involving a Massachusetts college team) and MGM Springfield.

**First-in-US bettor-limitation transparency rule.** Adopted 5-0 on 26 Feb 2026 and effective 1 Jun 2026, operators that limit an account must tell the patron why and which markets are affected (205 CMR 238.30(11)); 205 CMR 255 play-management (bettor-set limits, monthly notifications) goes to final adoption on 5 Nov 2026. This directly constrains the risk-management playbook that underpins 10%+ holds.

**Responsible-gambling and advertising rules are strict and statutory.** Minimum age 21; no wagering on in-state college teams outside tournaments of four-plus teams; no high-school events; credit-card funding of sports accounts prohibited [per 23N, unverified this session]; MGC advertising code (205 CMR 256) bars targeting under-21s and college campuses; unified Voluntary Self-Exclusion across casinos and sports; GameSense and PlayMyWay at casinos. A 'Youth Sports Betting Safety Coalition' run by the AG adds political pressure.

**Lottery has gone digital, adding a state-owned online competitor.** The Massachusetts Lottery launched iLottery (online tickets and e-instants, 21+, Aristocrat Interactive platform) on 27 Jul 2026, two years after FY25 budget authorisation. The Lottery is already one of the largest per-capita in the US (FY sales and profit figures not verified in this session) and will now compete for the same mobile wallet as sports and any future iGaming.

**DFS is shrinking as pick'em migrates to sportsbooks.** September 2026 gross fantasy receipts $11.5m (-35% YoY), net adjusted receipts $1.66m (-42%), tax $0.25m at 15%. In Sept 2025 DraftKings was $9.3m of $17.8m gross, PrizePicks $3.8m, Underdog $1.7m; the 2026 report no longer itemises operators in the summary.

**Read-through for B2Tech: a licence is theoretically obtainable, a business is not.** Entry would require either an untethered Category 3 award through a reopened MGC process or a tethered skin from Encore/MGM/the racetracks, a $5m fee, 20% GGR tax with no promo deduction, a limit-notification regime, and a market where the top two hold 78.5% of revenue and the #3–#7 share $127m of 9M revenue between them. Massachusetts is a market to serve via B2B/platform supply to an incumbent or to monitor for iGaming (2027+), not to enter as a B2C sportsbook.

segments.name: Sports wagering — online (Category 3) and retail
segments.headline: Handle +2.0% to $5.99bn, revenue +6.0% to $611m on a 10.2% hold; DraftKings/FanDuel hold 78.5% of revenue and the only share mover is Fanatics.
narrative: The MGC's September 2026 report, summed across Jan–Sep, gives 9M 2026 wagers settled of $5,994.3m, up 2.0% on the $5,877.1m in the September 2025 report (unrevised; operators restate small amounts — Sept 2025 handle was later revised from $800.26m to $800.46m). Online handle was $5,927.0m (+2.3%) and retail $67.3m (-19.4%). Monthly handle ran $813m in January, dipped to a 2026 low of $571m in August and rebounded to $773m in September with the NFL — but September was still 3.4% below the record $800m of September 2025. The quarterly pattern (Q1 -1.4%, Q2 +2.5%, Q3 +5.5%) shows modest re-acceleration, helped by the comparison base rather than any obvious new demand driver.

Taxable sports wagering revenue — the statutory GGR measure (gross receipts less winnings paid and federal excise; promotional credits are not deductible) — was $611.4m, +6.0%, on a 10.20% hold versus 9.82% in 9M 2025. The spread between revenue and handle growth is entirely hold: Q1 hold 10.36%, Q2 10.73% (yet revenue -1.0% YoY on a tough comp), Q3 9.49% (+17.7% on a weak September 2025 when hold was 6.5%). September 2026 revenue of $71.2m (+36.0%) and tax of $14.2m (+36.1%) therefore say more about results and parlay mix than about market expansion. FY2025 revenue was $841.7m on $8,529m handle (9.87% hold); LTM to September 2026 is $876.2m on $8,646m.

Operator structure is the defining feature. DraftKings settled $2,966.8m of 9M handle (49.5%) for $312.3m revenue (50.8%) at a 10.5% hold, paying $62.5m tax; FanDuel $1,494.7m (24.9%) for $169.8m (27.6%) at 11.4%. Together the two hold 74.5% of handle and 78.5% of revenue. Fanatics (tethered to Plainridge Park) is the only operator gaining meaningfully — handle +34.5% to $592.7m (9.9%), revenue +43% to $49.7m — at an 8.4% hold that suggests it is still buying share. BetMGM slipped 3.2% to $460.2m (7.7%); Caesars grew 10.1% to $204.4m but at a 6.8% hold earns only 2.3% of revenue; theScore Bet (Penn's replacement for ESPN Bet from late 2025) fell 11.9% to $167.0m; Bally Bet is sub-scale at $37.2m. The five books outside the duopoly shared $127.1m of revenue over nine months — roughly $25m each on average, before 20% tax and marketing.

Retail is a rounding error and shrinking. The three casino sportsbooks (Encore $33.1m handle, Plainridge $24.8m, MGM Springfield $9.4m) took $67.3m for $5.2m revenue; MGM Springfield booked zero taxable revenue in several months as negative results were carried forward under 23N. No Category 2 (racetrack/simulcast) retail sportsbook is reporting revenue. Retail matters only because each casino licence carries up to two online skins and the racetracks one each — the tether route by which Caesars, BetMGM, Fanatics and theScore Bet are in the market.

Demand-side rules shape the product set: bettors must be 21+, in-state college teams are off-limits outside tournaments of four or more teams, high-school events are banned, and the MGC's event catalog is enforced wager-by-wager (officiating markets such as soccer cards have been prohibited since December 2023). From 1 Jun 2026 any account that is limited must receive a notice stating the reason and the markets affected — Fanatics is already facing a non-compliance briefing on this. For an operator, the implication is that Massachusetts' 10%+ holds are being earned under a regulator that is actively policing the tools used to protect that hold.

Commercially, Massachusetts is a high-ARPU, low-growth state: ~$845 of handle per resident over nine months (estimate, ~7.1m population) with handle growth below US averages. The incremental opportunity for a new Category 3 entrant is the ~21% of revenue not held by DraftKings/FanDuel, in competition with four well-funded national brands, at a 20% GGR tax and with a $5m five-year licence fee [fee unverified this session]. Absent a differentiated product or a casino-tether partnership, the economics do not clear.

segments.name: Land-based casinos — Encore Boston Harbor, MGM Springfield, Plainridge Park
segments.headline: 9M GGR $879.8m (-2.4%) and tax $252.6m (-2.0%); Encore's September slump (-22%) drags an otherwise flat market.
narrative: Massachusetts' three licensed properties generated $879.8m of table-and-slot GGR in 9M 2026, down 2.4% from $901.8m, with taxes of $252.6m (-2.0%). Encore Boston Harbor (Wynn; Region A Category 1) remains 60.2% of the market at $529.2m but fell 4.7%; MGM Springfield (Region B Category 1) grew 1.1% to $214.6m; Plainridge Park Casino (Penn; the single Category 2 slots-only parlor) grew 1.1% to $136.0m. FY2025 casino GGR was $1,195m and LTM to September 2026 is $1,173m — the land-based base has been flat around $1.2bn for four years (September GGR: 2022 $95.8m, 2023 $93.8m, 2024 $92.1m, 2025 $95.7m, 2026 $82.7m).

September 2026 was conspicuously weak: total GGR $82.7m (-13.6%), the lowest September since the pandemic-restricted 2020, with Encore at $46.1m (-22.1%) — table GGR $19.1m versus $23.9m and slots $26.9m versus $35.3m a year earlier. MGM Springfield was $22.0m (-1.2%) and Plainridge $14.6m (+2.4%). The MGC's report is purely statistical and gives no explanation; a one-month table-hold swing cannot explain a 24% slot decline, so this warrants checking for property-specific disruption before extrapolating. Monthly 2026 GGR otherwise ran $92m–$108m, peaking in March ($107.8m) and May ($105.9m).

The tax structure is punitive by US standards and asymmetric: Category 1 resorts pay 25% of GGR, the Category 2 slots parlor 49%. Plainridge therefore remitted $66.7m on $136.0m of GGR in 9M 2026, more than MGM Springfield's $53.6m on $214.6m; Encore paid $132.3m. The blended effective rate is 28.7%. Casino tax is allocated by statute across local aid, transportation, education, debt reduction and the Public Health Trust Fund (allocation chart published on the MGC revenue page; percentages not reproduced here).

Licensing is closed. The Expanded Gaming Act (2011) capped the Commonwealth at three resort-casino licences (one per region) and one slots parlor; Region C (south-east) was never awarded, and the Mashpee Wampanoag tribal project that complicated it has not produced a casino. Category 1 licences were $85m for 15 years and the Category 2 licence $25m for five years [fee/term figures unverified this session], so the first resort-casino renewals fall in 2033–34 (MGM Springfield opened Aug 2018, Encore Jun 2019) while Plainridge is on a rolling five-year cycle. There is no realistic greenfield land-based entry for a new operator; the only route is M&A of an existing licensee.

For an online-first operator the land-based segment matters in two ways: each casino licence carries up to two online sports skins (the tether route) and, if Chapter 23O is ever enacted, the shelved H.4431 text would have restricted iGaming licences to the existing casino licensees — making a casino partnership the likely gateway to any future online casino market.

segments.name: Lottery, DFS and the unregulated fringe (iLottery, sweepstakes, prediction markets)
segments.headline: iLottery live since 27 Jul 2026, DFS shrinking (-42% net receipts in Sep), sweepstakes untouched, Kalshi enjoined pending the SJC.
narrative: The Massachusetts State Lottery — historically one of the highest per-capita lotteries in the US and the state's largest gambling revenue source (FY sales and net-profit figures were not verified in this session and are omitted) — launched online sales and e-instant games on 27 Jul 2026 on an Aristocrat Interactive platform, two years after the FY2025 budget authorised iLottery and after slipping from a late-2025 target. Play is restricted to 21+, aligning with casino and sports rules. The practical effect is a state-owned digital competitor for the casual mobile wallet in a state with no legal online casino; its revenue is not reported through the MGC and does not appear in the figures above.

Daily fantasy sports is regulated by registration with the MGC and taxed at 15% of net adjusted gross fantasy receipts under the 2022 sports wagering law. September 2026 gross fantasy receipts were $11.5m (-35.4% YoY), net adjusted receipts $1.66m (-42.5%) and tax $0.25m; in September 2025 DraftKings accounted for $9.3m of $17.8m gross receipts, PrizePicks $3.8m and Underdog $1.7m. The decline is consistent with pick'em-style products migrating into licensed sportsbooks' parlay menus. DFS is a sub-$5m-a-year tax line and no longer a strategic channel.

Sweepstakes-model casinos are not regulated by the MGC, were not addressed when H.4431 was sent to study in March 2026, and remain accessible — trade sources count 25+ sites. The Attorney General issued cease-and-desist letters to two offshore casino/sports operators in June 2025, signalling appetite to act under existing law, but no sweepstakes-specific statute or enforcement wave emerged in 2026. This is the de facto 'online casino' in Massachusetts today, untaxed and unmeasured.

Prediction markets are the most important fringe issue. AG Campbell sued KalshiEX in September 2025, alleging unlicensed sports wagering dressed as event contracts (moneyline, spread and totals contracts promoted on TV and social media). Suffolk Superior Court granted a preliminary injunction on 20 Jan 2026 requiring Kalshi to stop accepting sports contracts from Massachusetts customers until licensed by the MGC, and denied an emergency stay in February; Kalshi's appeal was argued before the Supreme Judicial Court on 4 May 2026, with a bipartisan coalition of 38 attorneys general filing in support of the Commonwealth. The SJC's decision could not be verified as of 6 Nov 2026. If upheld, Massachusetts becomes a template state for excluding CFTC-regulated sports contracts; if reversed, a zero-tax, no-licence competitor re-enters against a 20%-taxed licensed market.

For an operator, the fringe cuts both ways: the AG's posture protects licensed handle from prediction markets, but the same office frames all sports betting as a public-health harm and backs the Keenan bill's restrictions — the enforcement energy that removes Kalshi is the same energy that proposes a 51% tax.

If upheld, Massachusetts becomes a template for excluding CFTC-regulated sports contracts; if reversed, a no-licence competitor re-enters against a 20%-taxed market.

segments.name: Licensing and tax regime
segments.headline: Capped, closed licensing; GGR-based taxes of 20%/15% (sports), 25%/49% (casino), 15% (DFS); S.302 would take online sports to 51%.
narrative: Two statutes define the market. The Expanded Gaming Act of 2011 (G.L. c.23K) created the five-member Massachusetts Gaming Commission (chair Jordan Maynard, appointed by Governor Healey in October 2024) and authorised up to three Category 1 resort casinos — one per region — and one Category 2 slots parlor; only Regions A and B were licensed. An Act to Regulate Sports Wagering (H.5164, signed 10 Aug 2022; G.L. c.23N) created three sports licence classes: Category 1 (the casinos; retail plus up to two online skins each), Category 2 (racetracks/simulcast facilities; retail plus one skin) and Category 3 (untethered online, capped at seven). Retail launched 31 Jan 2023 and online 10 Mar 2023. The law permits 15 online operators (8 tethered, 7 untethered); seven are live, implying material unused capacity should the MGC reopen applications [slot arithmetic unverified this session]. Sports licences run five years at a $5m fee [unverified this session], so the first renewals fall in 2028.

Tax bases are gross-revenue measures with no promotional deduction. For sports, 'adjusted gross sports wagering receipts' is total gross receipts less winnings paid and federal excise (0.25% of handle); the MGC glossary reproduces this definition from c.23N §3. Where a month is negative, the operator carries the loss forward against later months — visible in MGM Springfield's zero-tax months. Rates are 20% for Category 3 online and 15% for Category 1/2 retail; 9M 2026 collections were $121.2m online and $0.8m retail. Casino GGR is taxed at 25% (Category 1) and 49% (Category 2); DFS at 15% of net adjusted receipts. Sports tax is distributed by statute to the General Fund, Gaming Local Aid, Workforce Investment Trust, Public Health Trust and Youth Development funds (MGC publishes the split as a chart; percentages not verified this session).

The live legislative threat is S.302, Senator John Keenan's 'An Act addressing economic, health and social harms caused by sports betting' (the 'Bettor Health Act'). As reported out of committee 5-0 in March 2026 it would raise the online rate from 20% to 51% (matching New York, Rhode Island and New Hampshire), prohibit proposition and in-game wagers, bar sports betting advertising during televised games, and require affordability assessments tied to account balances; trade reports also cite a $1,000 daily wager cap (secondary source, lower reliability). No enactment was found before the formal session ended on 31 Jul 2026 [status unverified this session]. A static calculation on FY2025 revenue of $842m implies state sports tax rising from ~$168m to ~$430m (estimate) — but the product bans would shrink the base, since parlays and props are the source of the 10%+ hold.

iGaming legislation (H.4431, Rep. David Muradian) would have added Chapter 23O and limited online casino licences to the existing casino operators via the MGC; the Joint Committee on Economic Development and Emerging Technologies sent it to study unanimously on 16 Mar 2026, effectively ending it for the 2025–26 session. Supporters framed it as having 'started the conversation'; realistically the earliest enactment is the 2027–28 session, with the Lottery's new iLottery and problem-gambling concerns as headwinds and the state's budget appetite as the tailwind.

For B2Tech the regime means: (1) a B2C sports licence is a $5m, five-year, 20%-GGR proposition with a credible path to 51% and product restrictions; (2) a casino tether is the only route to a future iGaming licence as currently drafted; (3) the regulator's 2026 enforcement cadence — penalties of $5,000–$60,000 are small, but public and frequent — adds compliance cost disproportionate to the revenue available outside the duopoly.

segments.name: Payments, responsible gambling, advertising and enforcement
segments.headline: Credit cards barred, 21+, first-in-US limit-notice rule from 1 Jun 2026, and an enforcement docket that touches every major operator.
narrative: Funding rules are statutory and conservative. Sports wagering accounts cannot be funded by credit card [per c.23N; not re-verified this session]; deposits run through debit, ACH/online banking, PayPal-type wallets, prepaid cards and cash at casino cages. There is no mobile-money dimension; the practical constraint is that geolocation must place the bettor inside Massachusetts at the time of the wager (BetMGM faces a 5 Nov 2026 briefing for allegedly accepting out-of-state wagers under c.23N §13(b) and 205 CMR 243/247), and that proxy wagering is prohibited (c.23N §11(a); 205 CMR 248.17) — the FanDuel briefing on the same agenda follows a podcaster's on-air admission that a relative bet through his account, which FanDuel self-reported and voided.

Responsible-gambling architecture is unified across verticals: one Voluntary Self-Exclusion list covering casinos, sports or both; GameSense advisors and the PlayMyWay slot-budgeting tool at the casinos; mandatory play-management tools online. The MGC went further than any US regulator on 26 Feb 2026 by adopting, 5-0, a requirement (205 CMR 238.30(11)) that operators who limit a patron's wagering must notify them, state the reason and identify the affected markets, with notices due from 1 Jun 2026; Fanatics is already cited for alleged non-compliance. On 5 Nov 2026 the Commission votes final adoption of amended 205 CMR 255 (play management), moving the limit-reminder cadence to monthly/30 days. The Keenan bill would add affordability checks against account balances and, per trade reports, a daily wager cap.

Advertising is governed by 205 CMR 256: no content appealing to or depicting under-21s, no advertising on college campuses or through college partnerships, mandatory problem-gambling messaging, and restrictions on inducement language. The AG's Youth Sports Betting Safety Coalition (formed March 2024) and S.302's proposed ban on ads during televised games indicate the direction of travel is tighter. Promotional mechanics are also policed: Fanatics' refer-a-friend bonuses are alleged to breach 205 CMR 247.09(4).

Enforcement is routine rather than episodic. The MGC's 2026 enforcement table (last updated 24 Aug 2026) lists 13 sports wagering penalties, all event-catalog breaches, from $5,000 to $25,000 (MGM Springfield $25,000 on 22 Jun 2026; Caesars $10,000 on 12 Mar 2026), following a $60,000 BetMGM penalty in December 2025 that bundled six matters including 2,564 prohibited soccer-card wagers. The 5 Nov 2026 meeting (No. 601) adds Caesars (unauthorised event; unauthorised event involving a Massachusetts collegiate team) and MGM Springfield (unapproved offering) penalty votes. Fines are immaterial financially but each generates a public decision and press cycle, and repeat findings feed directly into the 2028 licence-renewal record.

Operator implication: compliance in Massachusetts is a standing cost centre — event-catalog controls, geofencing, promotional-term review and limit-notice workflows — that scales with headcount, not revenue. For a sub-5%-share operator the fixed compliance load is a meaningful drag on a state that would yield perhaps $15–25m of annual GGR.

highlights.text: Premium monetisation: 9M 2026 hold of 10.2% (FanDuel 11.4%, DraftKings 10.5%) on a GGR tax of 20% leaves one of the better net margins among large US states — provided the product mix (parlays/props) survives S.302.

Regulatory moat against prediction markets: the AG's preliminary injunction against Kalshi (Jan 2026), backed by 38 state AGs at the SJC, protects licensed handle from a zero-tax competitor if upheld.

Unused licence capacity: the statute allows 15 online operators but only 7 are live; tethered skins at Encore (1), MGM Springfield (1) and the two racetracks appear available, giving a B2B/skin route without a competitive RFA [slot count unverified].

Share is still moving below the duopoly: Fanatics grew handle 34.5% to 9.9% share in 9M 2026 and Caesars +10.1%, showing a tethered challenger can take share from BetMGM/theScore Bet with product and loyalty rather than promo spend.

Future iGaming optionality via casino partnership: the shelved H.4431 would have confined online casino licences to the three casino licensees; a tether with Encore or MGM Springfield positions an operator for a 2027–28 reopening.

Stable, transparent regulator: monthly operator-level handle/revenue/tax disclosure, a fixed five-member commission, and predictable rulemaking cycles reduce execution risk relative to emerging markets.

lowlights.text: Tax-rate cliff: S.302 (51% online tax, prop/in-play ban, TV ad ban, affordability checks) cleared committee 5-0 in March 2026 and will almost certainly be refiled in January 2027; at 51% the #3–#7 operators' combined 9M revenue of $127m would not cover marketing and compliance.
Growth has stalled: handle +2.0% in 9M 2026 and -3.4% in September; Q1 was negative. The 6% revenue growth is hold-driven and reverses with results — Q2 revenue was -1.0% YoY.
Duopoly lock-in: DraftKings (home state) and FanDuel hold 74.5% of handle and 78.5% of revenue; the remaining five brands average ~$25m of 9M revenue each before 20% tax.

The most interventionist US regulator on risk management: mandatory limit-notification (from 1 Jun 2026), play-management rules, event-catalog penalties on every operator in 2026, and an AG who frames sports betting as a public-health harm.
No iGaming before 2027–28 at the earliest, while the Lottery's iLottery (live 27 Jul 2026) and unregulated sweepstakes sites absorb the casual digital casino wallet in the meantime.
Land-based weakness: casino GGR -2.4% in 9M 2026 and Encore -22% in September with no regulator commentary — relevant to any tether partner's health and to the 49%/25% tax base the state relies on.

Kalshi reversal risk: if the SJC sides with Kalshi, a federally-regulated, untaxed sports-contract venue returns to Massachusetts against a 20%-taxed licensed market — the outcome was unverifiable as of 6 Nov 2026.

forecast.intro: The 9M 2026 print moves the Massachusetts base case from 'growth market' to 'mature, hold-driven market': sports handle of $5.99bn (+2.0%) and revenue of $611m (+6.0%) versus a prior-year pace of double-digit growth, with the land-based segment flat-to-down ($880m, -2.4%). The division driving the change is online sports — handle growth of 2.3% is the slowest since launch — while the swing in revenue is almost entirely a 38bp hold uplift. The moving parts for the next 12–24 months are regulatory rather than commercial: the fate of S.302 (51% tax, prop/in-play ban), the SJC's Kalshi ruling, the 2028 licence-renewal cycle, and whether iGaming is refiled in the 2027–28 session.

forecast.view: Our independent view: **revenue grows low-to-mid single digits, not volume.** We expect FY2026 sports handle of roughly $8.5–8.7bn (estimate, ~flat to +2%) and taxable revenue of $880–900m (estimate), with Q4 dependent on NFL/NBA results; casino GGR finishes around $1.17–1.19bn (estimate). **Margins for incumbents stay attractive** at a 20% GGR tax and 10% hold, but we assign a meaningful probability (we would say roughly one-in-three over two sessions) that Massachusetts legislates some combination of a higher rate and product restrictions by 2028, given a Senate committee that voted 5-0, an AG aligned with the sponsor, and a 2028 licence-renewal window that gives the legislature leverage. **Leverage/structure direction:** expect further consolidation to five or six online brands — theScore Bet and Bally Bet are sub-scale — and expect any new entrant to arrive via a casino tether rather than a fresh Category 3 award. **iGaming**: not before 2027–28; the Lottery's iLottery and the AG's public-health framing make even that uncertain, and any bill will likely restrict licences to casino licensees. **Kalshi**: an SJC affirmance would be the most valuable regulatory development of 2026 for licensees; a reversal would be a 2027 handle headwind. For B2Tech, the actionable positions are B2B platform/content supply to an incumbent or tethered partner, and a watching brief on Chapter 23O — not a B2C sportsbook launch.
watch: Supreme Judicial Court decision in Commonwealth v. KalshiEX (argued 4 May 2026): affirmance locks prediction markets out; reversal reopens a zero-tax competitor.
Refiling of S.302 (Bettor Health Act) in January 2027 and whether the House and Governor Healey engage — the 51% rate and prop/in-play ban would reset operator economics and the hold structure.

Q4 2026 / FY2026 MGC revenue reports (December report due ~mid-Jan 2027): whether handle re-accelerates with the NFL/NBA season or Q1-2026-style declines return; whether Encore Boston Harbor's September slump persists.
MGC 2027–28 licence-renewal process for the 2023 Category 1/3 sports licences (five-year terms) — renewal conditions could codify limit-notification, affordability or advertising requirements.
Reintroduction of an iGaming bill (Chapter 23O) in the 2027–28 session and its licence-eligibility language (casino licensees only vs open).
Sweepstakes-casino action by the AG or legislature, and iLottery's first reported sales — both affect the size of the unregulated/adjacent online casino wallet.
MGC enforcement outcomes on 5 Nov 2026 (Fanatics, BetMGM, FanDuel, Caesars, MGM Springfield) and any escalation from five-figure penalties to licence conditions.
